messages.text: Here, {gift_item}. Straight aim starts before the bow is drawn.
Take {gift_item}. If trouble comes, I would like you ready for it.

openings.text: Mind the fletching table. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to balancing arrows true, then.

lines.text: Clean feathers and straight shafts make trouble keep its distance.
A good bow hears trouble before the bell does.
Missed shots teach loudly, especially when everyone heard you brag first.
Mind the fletching table. Straight arrows do not happen by accident.
A crooked feather makes a promise the arrow cannot keep.
Distance changes everything. Trouble looks smaller until it arrives.
I once threw away a whole bundle because one shaft taught me suspicion.
A fletcher joke should fly straight. Mine wobble honestly.
That was blunt enough to disappoint an arrow.
The best warning is the one that reaches trouble before trouble reaches us.
Aim is not just the hand. It is patience deciding not to flinch.
There are nights when the bell rings and every arrow feels too few.
Keep testing patience and you will learn how warnings travel.

pacify.text: Fine. I will unstring the anger, but only this once.
That does not fly far enough. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
No. Some targets stay marked until trust returns.
